about: Night cycling along a park connector

lines.text: After the sun sets, the park connector near my home becomes a different
place. The heat of the day is gone, and the path are lit
lines.note: Agreement: 'the path' is one thing, so it is 'is lit'.

lines.text: by rows of soft yellow lamps. My father and I have cycle there
every Friday night since I was twelve. We usually set off on nine
lines.note: Preposition: a clock time takes 'at' — 'at nine o’clock'.

lines.text: o’clock, when most joggers have left. The route follows the canal for a hour
lines.note: Article: 'hour' starts with a vowel sound, so it is 'an hour'.

lines.text: before it reaches the sea. On clear nights, we can see ships waiting
far out in the dark water. Cycling at night is peaceful, so it
lines.note: Connector: the two ideas contrast, so it is 'but', not 'so'.

lines.text: also demands care. We wear bright vests and fix lights to our bicycle
lines.note: Plural: there are two riders, so it is 'our bicycles'.

lines.text: so that other riders can see us clear. My father always reminds me
lines.note: Word form: 'see' is a verb, so it takes the adverb 'clearly'.

lines.text: to slow down at bends, where a careless cyclist once knocks him over.
lines.note: Tense: it happened once in the past, so it is 'knocked'.

lines.text: When we finally stop for a drink, I feel calmer than I have
all week, and I am already looking forward to the next ride.
